task_title: Durable fix: prevent ci-owner lock deadlock (reaper lane + 422 crash fix + liveness TTL)

plan_review.notes: Option A re-scoped this from 3🍎 to 4🍎 and ran an ADVERSARIAL separate-model plan review that red-teamed the original liveness-binding design and enumerated three approaches: (1) infer session liveness from head workflow_runs (the originally-planned signal), (2) an actor/name-attributable copilot-swe-agent run signal, (3) no-run-inference: freeze progressAt on the lease-reaper stale-retry so the existing 2-attempt ceiling becomes a true wall-clock TTL. VERDICT = DIVERGENT (major_fork): approach (1) is UNSAFE because unrelated CI/merge-train/sweep runs AND the reaper's own reconcile dispatch share the head SHA, so any liveness inference reads true forever and makes the lock immortal (the exact deadlock being fixed); approach (2) has no reliable per-session attribution at reconcile time. Adopted approach (3). The 1 major concern (unsafe liveness inference) was resolved by re-architecting to the freeze-progressAt/attempt-carry design now implemented in reconcile.mjs.

rounds.notes: Dedicated deep code review of the full diff (reconcile.mjs freeze/attempt-carry path, router.mjs identifyReapablePrs predicate + selectReaperBatch, and the four new tests). Traced the freeze+attempt-carry to a guaranteed release within ≤3 sweeps, confirmed the null/undefined predicate ordering, and verified the new tests are non-vacuous. No concerns.

claude-opus-4.8: no significant issues. gemini-3.1-pro-preview: one HIGH finding — selectReaperBatch rotated the reapable list to prevent starvation, but the input order derives from GitHub's updated_at-desc pull feed which churns as reaping bumps a PR's updated_at, so rotating an unstable list breaks the cross-window fairness guarantee (tail PRs could starve) and the original test fed a static array so it passed vacuously. Adjudication (claude-opus-4.8): gemini's finding is VALID (Opus reviewed the test-as-written; Gemini correctly identified the real-world input is not static). Remedy: stable-sort by PR number before rotating so the batch is a pure function of the input SET plus the time window.

Confirmation re-review of the stable-sort fix + strengthened test by two distinct models. Both confirm: the fix fully resolves the churn/starvation concern with no new bug (non-mutating spread, correct numeric comparator, empty/single-element safe), the added order-independence assertion (ascending vs shuffled vs descending yield the same batch for a fixed now) is genuine and load-bearing (verified it fails without the sort), and the runFromEnv call site is unchanged. No findings.
